In mathematical [[invariant theory]], a '''perpetuant''' is informally an irreducible covariant of a form or infinite degree. More precisely, the dimension of the space of irreducible covariants of given degree and weight for a binary form stabilizes provided the degree of the form is larger than the weight of the covariant, and the elements of this space are called perpetuants. Perpetuants were introduced and named by {{harvs|txt|last=Sylvester|year=1882|loc=p.105}}.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Sylvester |first1=James Joseph |title=On Subvariants, i.e. Semi-Invariants to Binary Quantics of an Unlimited Order |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=79–136 |year=1882 |publisher=The Johns Hopkins University Press |doi=10.2307/2369536 |issn=0002-9327 |jstor=2369536}}</ref> {{harvs|txt|last=MacMahon|year1=1884|year2=1885|year3=1894}}<ref>{{Citation |last1=MacMahon |first1=P. A. |title=On Perpetuants |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=7 |issue=1 |pages=26–46 |year=1884 |publisher=The Johns Hopkins University Press |doi=10.2307/2369457 |issn=0002-9327 |jstor=2369457}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last1=MacMahon |first1=P. A. |title=A Second Paper on Perpetuants |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=7 |issue=3 |pages=259–263 |year=1885 |publisher=The Johns Hopkins University Press |doi=10.2307/2369271 |issn=0002-9327 |jstor=2369271}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last1=MacMahon |first1=P. A. |title=The Perpetuant Invariants of Binary Quantics |journal=Proc. London Math. Soc. |volume=26 |issue=1 |pages=262–284 |year=1894 |url=https://zenodo.org/record/1433386 |doi=10.1112/plms/s1-26.1.262}}</ref> and {{harvs|txt|last=Stroh|year=1890}}<ref>{{Citation |last1=Stroh |first1=E. |title=Ueber die symbolische Darstellung der Grundsyzyganten einer binären Form sechster Ordnung und eine Erweiterung der Symbolik von Clebsch |journal=[[Mathematische Annalen]] |volume=36 |issue=2 |pages=262–303 |year=1890 |url=https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/id/PPN235181684_0036?tify={%22pages%22:[2],%22panX%22:0.802,%22panY%22:0.529,%22view%22:%22info%22,%22zoom%22:0.489} |publisher=Springer Berlin / Heidelberg |doi=10.1007/BF01207843 |s2cid=121641107 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> classified the perpetuants. {{harvtxt|Elliott|1907}} describes the early history of perpetuants and gives an annotated bibliography.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Elliott |first1=Edwin Bailey |title=On Perpetuants and Contra-Perpetuants |journal=Proc. London Math. Soc. |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=228–246 |year=1907 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=a7xLAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA228 |doi=10.1112/plms/s2-4.1.228 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

MacMahon conjectured and Stroh proved that the dimension of the space of perpetuants of degree ''n''>2 and weight ''w'' is the coefficient of ''x''<sup>''w''</sup> of 
:<math>\frac{x^{2^{n-1}-1}}{(1-x^2)(1-x^3)\cdots(1-x^n)}</math>
For ''n''=1 there is just one perpetuant, of weight 0, and for ''n''=2 the number is given by the coefficient of ''x''<sup>''w''</sup> of ''x''<sup>2</sup>/(1-''x''<sup>2</sup>).

There are very few papers after about 1910 discussing perpetuants; Littlewood<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1944-02-04 |title=Invariant theory, tensors and group characters |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsta.1944.0001 |journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences |language=en |volume=239 |issue=807 |pages=305–365 |doi=10.1098/rsta.1944.0001 |issn=0080-4614|url-access=subscription }}</ref> is one of the few exceptions. {{harvs|last1=Kraft|last2=Procesi|year=2020}} exhibited an explicit base of the space of perpetuants.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kraft |first=Hanspeter |last2=Procesi |first2=Claudio |date=2020-03-11 |title=Perpetuants: A Lost Treasure |url=https://doi.org/10.1093/imrn/rnaa032 |journal=International Mathematics Research Notices |volume=2021 |issue=5 |pages=3597–3632 |arxiv=1810.01131 |doi=10.1093/imrn/rnaa032 |issn=1073-7928}}</ref>
